Messages.Author: Petri Wessman
Messages.Body:
We were playing a twisted variant of Jyhad last night and some general
questions came up:

+ Can you commit suicide (transfer all of your pool to a minion with a
Blood Doll, for example)?

+ Archon: the card reads "any vampire". Can a meth with an Archon
attack his/her own vampires?

+ Malkavian Prank: the card says "each Methuselah". Does the meth
playing the card also take 1-4 blood and "guess" the amount?

//Petri

Messages.Author: Neil Bernstein
Messages.Body:
Petri Wessman (Petri....@hut.fi) wrote:
: We were playing a twisted variant of Jyhad last night and some general
: questions came up:

: + Can you commit suicide (transfer all of your pool to a minion with a
: Blood Doll, for example)?

This is a time-honored practice in our group (though a more usual way
to do it is by transferring to uncontrolled vampires). Sort of like
mana-burn suicides in That Other Game.

: + Archon: the card reads "any vampire". Can a meth with an Archon
: attack his/her own vampires?

Why not? I can think of several situations in which I'd like to see
one of my own vampires torpored, and if my opponent keeps dodging out
of the way I might want to do it myself.

: + Malkavian Prank: the card says "each Methuselah". Does the meth

: playing the card also take 1-4 blood and "guess" the amount?

Nope. The Malk player only joins the party in Game of Malkav.

- Neil

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Petri....@hut.fi (Petri Wessman) writes:

>We were playing a twisted variant of Jyhad last night and some general
>questions came up:

>+ Can you commit suicide (transfer all of your pool to a minion with a
> Blood Doll, for example)?

Of course. Calling a Domain Challenge to oust yourself as well as
your Prey is not unheard of in my group. And there's the old example
of ousting yourself by equipping with Vast Wealth and drawing an
equipment that costs too much.

>+ Archon: the card reads "any vampire". Can a meth with an Archon
> attack his/her own vampires?

Well, A, it has errata that the attack is a (D) action, and as
such cannot be directed toward your own cards. And, B, you can
never get into combat with nor Bleed yourself under any circumstances.

>+ Malkavian Prank: the card says "each Methuselah". Does the meth
> playing the card also take 1-4 blood and "guess" the amount?

Heh. I'm sure the answer is no. It says "guess how much is in each
Methuselah's hand", but it starts with "All *other* Methuselahs hold between
1 and 4 blood" [emphasis mine]. So, while you could guess for yourself, you
would not be holding anything - and so would gain or lose zero, respectively.

Good try, though :-)
--

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
L. Scott Johnson <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> wrote:

>>>...B, you can

>>>never get into combat with nor Bleed yourself under any circumstances.
>>Well, neither of those is technically impossible. The card set is just
>>engineered to avoid that sort of thing, is all.
>Eh?
>You have said "(D) actions cannot be directed at oneself unless card text
>indicates that it can be self-directed <4ar27a$q...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>".
>Was that a mistake?

No. As I said, the card set is just *engineered* to avoid attacking
your own minions, and a large part of that is making all attacks directed.

>And are you saying that some card may eventually allow me to attack
>my own minion? Combat with oneself is patently against the mechanics
>of the game.

It's against the design of the game, but not against the mechanics of the
game. While I doubt we would print a card that simply let you attack your
own minions, if someone found a tortured combination of three or four cards
that wound up letting you attack one of your own, there wouldn't be any
(meta)rule stopping you.

>As far as Bleeding yourself, that is a longstanding rule:

> 5) If an action card such as Computer Hacking provides a directed
> bleed, you may bleed any player other than yourself.

Again, it's a design issue, not a mechanics issue. While we don't intend
to ever let you flatly bleed yourself, there wouldn't be anything stopping
obscure card combos from allowing this.

Let me emphasize: I don't expect us to ever allow a player to attack his or
her own minions, or bleed his or her own pool. But that's purely a design
issue, not a mechanics issue.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

The card of which you speak is the Major Boon:
M:OOT
Play this card to take another Methuselah's blood pool loss due to a bleed
(must be at least 1 blood). Modifiers to the bleed can be played after you
play this card. In the future you can force the rescued Methuselah to take a
loss due to a bleed against you. This boon is then burned.

Nowhere in the text of the card does it state or imply that it cannot
be used against the methuselah you rescued, so I would have to say that it is
an exception to the rule. The 'deflection' type cards I was referring to are:
Deflection, Telepathic Misdirection...and maybe a couple of others which are
MINION cards, not master. Basically, what I am trying to say is that minions
are not powerful enough to redirect a bleed to the bleeding methuselah.
However, MASTERS (methuselahs) are powerful enough.

Messages.Author: Mike Kelly
Messages.Body:
The bleed is NOT being redirected. The other Methuselah is being forced to pay
for the bleed. YOU are still the one being bled, HE is the one paying.
